steps.title: Start with the destination
steps.question: What are we building?
explanation: Code Arena is a game where two sides solve the same programming Problem. A side is one player in 1v1, or two teammates in 2v2.
One Match contains three Rounds in the reference game. Each Round brings a new Problem. You will build the pieces in a separate practice folder before connecting them to your team’s app.

steps.title: Follow one Round
steps.question: What does a player do?
explanation: Read the Problem. Write a small program in the editor. Run the visible examples to find mistakes. Submit when you want the hidden tests to score your code.
At Reveal, both sides see the Round results. After the last Round, the game adds the scores and decides the winner.

steps.title: Give each part one job
steps.question: Where does the work happen?
explanation: The browser shows the editor and results. The server checks who may act and keeps the official Match state. The database saves accepted state.
A separate Judge runs player programs inside an isolated environment. Your browser and the Game server must not execute untrusted player code directly.

title: Know which folder is yours
why: You need a safe place to write before following any file instruction.
outcome: Tell the reference, practice, and team folders apart.

steps.title: Three different jobs
steps.question: Where will you write your code?
explanation: The coded game you already have is the reference. Read it to understand a decision and compare behavior.
Your practice folder will hold your own code. The team repository will be the final home when your friend creates it. You can begin without it.

steps.title: A root is a starting folder
steps.question: Why do instructions keep showing the root?
explanation: A relative path such as src/rule.ts starts inside a project root. The same path can exist in two different projects.
The workspace bar names which project you are using. The terminal command pwd shows the folder your terminal is currently inside. Check both before editing.

steps.title: Choose a home
steps.question: Your friend has no repo yet. Are you blocked?
explanation: No. A pure rule can be written and tested in practice first. A pure rule makes a decision from its inputs without needing a server or database.
Later, the same idea can move into a team-owned file. A practice test passing will not count as a team-repository test.
